svg.text: ARCHITECTURE LAB / REVISION 06 — RHYTHM, KIT AND CIRCUIT
Four reusable pieces plus swap-outs. The circuit below is provisional — the section is what is being signed off first.
All dimensions in metres on a 0.125 m grid (4 map units at 32 u/m). Colour identifies construction, not final materials.
R1 PLINTH
0 – 1.25 m · base kick, plinth, chamfer out
R2 PANEL
1.25 – 2.50 m · eye level, the only zone that swaps
R3 UPPER
2.50 – 3.75 m · chamfer, upper wall, ceiling
THE SECTION, IN BRIEF
Nine facets per half, in three reusable pieces. See architecture-lab-section.png for every dimension.
4.0 × 3.2 clear
Widest interior 6.00 m · crown 3.75 m · rib beam soffit 3.50 m.
Outward-rising facets are 63.43°, 56.31° and 51.34°; the 45° chamfers are all overhangs.
The kick is the single facet the player can stand on, so it is the
only one that has to beat the floor_max_angle default.
FLOOR, WALL and CEILING are three separate reusable brushes.
Mirror them for the far half. Any one can be swapped for a
special without touching the other two.
The RIB drops in every 4 m — four 1 m texture repeats — and
runs floor to ceiling; opposite toes define the 4.00 m clear lane.
The circuit below still carries revision 05 routing. Its numbers
are provisional until the section is signed off.
SPINE / WEST WALL ELEVATION — provisional routing at 4.0 m pitch
Ribs every 4.0 m — four 1 m texture repeats. The panel between them is what changes, not the section.
ALCOVE
4.0 × 3.2 T OPENING
to west branch
rib suppressed
2.0 × 2.0 CEILING HATCH RESERVED
Z (metres, north is negative)
WHY 4.0 m PITCH
One rib every four 1 m texture repeats, so the rib
always lands on a texture seam.
WHY A 3.75 m CROWN
6.00 wide, but the walking lane is still 4.00.
Rib beam soffit 3.50 clears the 3.2 envelope by 0.30.
LIGHT IS STILL OPEN
Deferred until the section is signed off. The ceiling
piece is the obvious carrier, as a swap-out.
BAY INSERT KIT — the section never changes, the bay does
Swap-outs replace the 1.25 – 2.50 m panel zone only, so the floor, ceiling and rib pieces are untouched.
PANEL
Flat panel behind the rib plane.
The quiet default. Cheapest bay.
GRILLE
Louvres set 0.125 m deeper.
Honest home for a wall hatch.
EQUIPMENT
Cabinets inside the panel zone.
Never crosses the rib plane.
RECESS
Full depth to floor, 0.50 m.
Standing cover. Plinth stops.
WINDOW
Sill 1.25, head 2.50, chamfered reveal.
Glazing 0.75 m outboard.
DOOR
2.00 × 2.46 DoorModule, centred.
Ribs are the wall returns.
PORTAL BAY
Two bays merged
by dropping one rib.
4.00 opening
5.50 m clear between flanking ribs · 0.75 bay + 0.50 rib = 1.25 m return each side
This is the systemic win: the rib rhythm satisfies the project’s “1 m of solid wall beyond a frame”
rule automatically, at every opening, without anyone measuring it. Single-bay doors serve side
rooms; portal bays carry main routes and junctions. It also gives openings a visible hierarchy.
CIRCUIT PLAN — one walk that exercises every part of the kit
rib / structure
bay infill
plinth
service insert
clear lane / alcove
glazing
opening
exterior volume
KEY
Spawn. The spine, ribs every 4 m.
Alcove bay — the section gives ground below 2 m.
Portal bay carrying the 4.0 × 3.2 T opening.
West branch, ending in a door bay + stub.
Sealed 2.0 × 2.0 ceiling hatch, between ribs, clear of light.
Corner — mitre outside, solid rib block inside.
Two window bays, outboard side only.
6 m portal bay ending in a 4.0 × 2.0 viewport.
Mars exterior: sealed, not traversable, one raking light.
THE WALK
Spawn, then north up the spine — the bays teach the rhythm
before anything unusual happens. The alcove is the first time
section gives ground. Judge it as cover, not decoration.
The T is a portal bay in the same rhythm: its flanking ribs
are the wall returns, for free.
The corner is the real test — the chamfers have to mitre — so
the knee gets a mitre outside and a solid rib block inside.
The end viewport is the one deliberate rule break.
BUILD ORDER — each stage is walkable and answers exactly one question
1 Spine only, panel bays throughout, flat neutral light.
2 Inserts, portal bay, T, corner, door bay.
3 Trough reveal lighting, alternating bays.
4 Mars volume, window bays, end viewport.
Does the 4.0 m rhythm read, and is 6.00 × 3.75 the right size?
Does the kit hold together, and does the corner actually resolve?
Do the panel swap-outs carry enough interest on their own?
Does the red light do the work — is a glimpse of Mars enough?
REVISION 06 / circuit routing provisional · the revision 05 stage 1 build is superseded · section detail in architecture-lab-section.png
